label: Ceasefires Currently in Force
contestNote: AUG 27 status — Gaza: nominally holding since Oct 2025 but near-daily strikes continue; Aug 23 strikes killed 3 more (incl. a 4-year-old) and Netanyahu/Katz threatened to 'intensify strikes' over kite/balloon launches from Gaza; Aug 25 the Board of Peace issued a rare dual warning — telling Hamas 'all militant activity in Gaza must stop' while telling Israel 'military action cannot extend beyond responding to genuine and imminent threats'; Aug 26 Board of Peace chair Mladenov told the UN Security Council a ceasefire collapse would be an irreversible 'point of no return,' crediting Hamas's first-ever agreement to hand over weapons while still criticizing Israel's strikes. Lebanon: Jun 26 Washington framework signed; 7th round Rome talks (Aug 4-6) produced a reported verification-country shortlist, but a Lebanese official denied Aug 13 that any such shortlist was agreed; Aug 20 US Treasury sanctions on a Hezbollah cash-smuggling network and re-designation of Hezbollah as an Iranian-Qods-Force proxy add fresh pressure on the disarmament sequencing dispute ahead of the next round in early Sep. Iran: Jun 17 Islamabad MOU's 60-day window EXPIRED Aug 17 with no comprehensive deal; Aug 20 Trump announced an 'economic D-Day,' and Aug 24 Treasury Secretary Bessent moved to unveil the sanctions package itself; but Aug 24-25 Pakistan's army chief Munir and Interior Min. Naqvi held 'highly positive' Tehran talks reviewing steps to restore the MOU. Yemen: 2022 UN truce framework under its worst strain since 2022 — Grundberg warned the UN Security Council Aug 13 that Yemen faces its greatest risk of renewed large-scale war since the 2022 truce. Ethiopia: worst breach yet of 2022 Pretoria agreement, fighting resumed near Sheraro Aug 1, with reports of de-escalation by Aug 2 but no formal reaffirmation of the ceasefire. Colombia: De la Espriella inaugurated Aug 7, formally winding down 'Total Peace' and launching a 90-day offensive; Aug 27 formalized the policy's end by ordering extradition of five former Total Peace negotiators to the US, declaring 'In my government, there will be no peace processes.' DRC-Rwanda: Doha track roadmap agreed Aug 23 after 5 days of Swiss-hosted talks (Aug 17-21) with US/Qatar/Togo/Switzerland/AU present — first real Doha-track progress in months, alongside the still-stalled Washington Accords track. Venezuela: government-opposition talks concluded a first round Aug 12 with judicial-reform and frozen-funds agreements; 1,046+ prisoners freed as of Aug 15. Ukraine: no ceasefire; Russia's Ryabkov said Aug 21 Moscow is open to 'new ideas' only if they match Putin's preconditions; Witkoff/Kushner postponed their planned first Kyiv visit Aug 24 amid intensified Russian strikes; POW-exchange channel remains the only functioning track. Sudan: Burhan pledged national-dialogue immunity Aug 15; AU Peace and Security Council delegation visited Khartoum Aug 15-16; Aug 22-23 a broad anti-war civilian coalition rejected Burhan's dialogue offer in Addis Ababa and proposed an alternative 'Peace Process We Want' roadmap. Syria: SDF formally dissolved into the Syrian army Aug 25, completing the Jan 29 integration accord — one of the year's clearer implementation successes.
deltaNote: Ethiopia Pretoria agreement breach (Aug 1), Yemen truce framework at gravest strain since 2022 (Aug 6-7), the Iran Islamabad MOU's 60-day window expiring without a deal (Aug 17), the Aug 20-24 US-Iran sanctions escalation, and Colombia's Aug 27 formal end of Total Peace pressure the 'in force' count; partly offset by Lebanon framework formalization (Jun 26), Gaza disarmament-mechanism agreement (Aug 17), the Aug 23 DRC-M23 Doha roadmap, and the Aug 25 Syria SDF-army merger completion; net -1 vs Jun 7 baseline

Ethiopia-Tigray Pretoria agreement suffers its worst breach yet (fighting near Sheraro, Aug 1) — added to collapsed list. Yemen 2022 truce framework at gravest risk of full collapse since inception — Grundberg told the UN Security Council Aug 13 that Yemen faces its greatest risk of renewed large-scale conflict since the April 2022 truce. Colombia Total Peace formally ended: the De la Espriella administration (inaugurated Aug 7) launched a 90-day offensive against armed groups, then on Aug 27 ordered extradition to the US of five individuals recognized as Total Peace negotiators, declaring 'In my government, there will be no peace processes.' Sudan Boulos-plan talks remain stalled — SAF/RSF gave incompatible responses (Jul 12-14) — and Aug 22-23 anti-war civilian forces formally rejected Burhan's alternative national-dialogue offer in Addis Ababa, proposing their own civilian-led roadmap instead. Lebanon-Israel verification-mechanism track complicated by Beirut's Aug 13 denial that any country shortlist was agreed, and further pressured by Aug 20 US sanctions on Hezbollah's financing network. Ukraine's Witkoff/Kushner shuttle track hit a further delay Aug 24 (postponed first Kyiv visit amid Russian strikes). Offsetting progress: DRC-Rwanda's Doha track posted its first real progress in months (Aug 23 roadmap agreement), and Syria's SDF completed its formal dissolution into the Syrian army Aug 25 — one of the clearest implementation successes of the year. Full list: Afghanistan (Doha), Sudan (Jeddah/Boulos plan stalled), Myanmar (ASEAN 5-pt still largely nominal despite Jul 12-16 re-engagement), Ethiopia-Tigray (Pretoria breached Aug 1), Colombia ELN/Total Peace (formally ended Aug 27, 2026), Libya LPDF, Gaza Phase II (disarmament-sequencing mechanism agreed Aug 17 but implementation contested after Aug 18, 23 strikes; Board of Peace dual warning Aug 25 and 'point of no return' warning Aug 26), Yemen (near-collapse Aug 2026), Iran-US Islamabad MOU (60-day window expired Aug 17, sanctions campaign unveiled Aug 24, revival talks Aug 24-25), Ukraine (no ceasefire; POW exchanges only functioning track; Witkoff/Kushner Kyiv visit postponed Aug 24).
